edition: 2021 (verified local teaching dataset; maintainer must check official OWASP project before delivery)
note: Category titles are summarised from OWASP. The short explanations, examples, impacts and prevention notes are student-friendly teaching text. Update this local file after an official new release; never scrape at runtime. Network access to official sources was unavailable in the build environment, so users must complete the documented release check before classroom use.

categories.name: Broken Access Control
categories.explanation: People can do something they should not be allowed to do.
categories.example: A learner changes a record URL and sees another user’s record.
categories.prevention: Check permissions on every request and deny by default.

categories.name: Cryptographic Failures
categories.explanation: Sensitive data is not protected properly.
categories.example: A site sends a password over an unencrypted connection.
categories.prevention: Use HTTPS and modern encryption; do not invent crypto.

categories.name: Injection
categories.explanation: Untrusted input changes the meaning of a command or query.
categories.example: A form value is treated as part of a database query.
categories.impact: Data loss, disclosure or control of a system.
categories.prevention: Validate input and use parameterised queries.

categories.name: Insecure Design
categories.explanation: A safety control was missing from the design, not just the code.
categories.example: A reset journey has no limit on repeated attempts.
categories.prevention: Threat-model features and design security controls early.

categories.name: Security Misconfiguration
categories.explanation: A setting is unsafe or left at its default.
categories.example: A production server shows detailed error pages.

categories.name: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
categories.explanation: A project uses software with known security problems.
categories.example: An old library has a published CVE.
categories.impact: Attackers may exploit a known weakness.

categories.name: Identification and Authentication Failures
categories.explanation: Identity checks or login protection are too weak.
categories.example: A service accepts easy-to-guess passwords without limits.
categories.prevention: Use MFA, safe password storage and rate limits.

categories.name: Software and Data Integrity Failures
categories.explanation: Code or data is trusted without checking it.
categories.example: A build downloads a package without verifying its source.
categories.prevention: Use signed, reviewed sources and protected pipelines.

categories.name: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
categories.explanation: Important events are not recorded or noticed.
categories.example: Repeated failed logins are neither logged nor reviewed.
categories.impact: Incidents take longer to detect and investigate.
categories.prevention: Log useful events and practise alert response.

categories.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
categories.explanation: A server fetches a URL chosen by a user without safe controls.
categories.example: An image-import tool requests an internal service address.
categories.impact: Access to internal systems or data.
categories.prevention: Allow-list destinations and isolate network access.
